raw_response:
Aiya, you want to know what I do this year? Same as every year, mostly. Thirty years on these fields, my hands know what to do.

I've got about ten mu and some. Six mu of it I do wheat-maize — plant wheat after the maize comes off in October, then the minute the wheat combine finishes in June I'm back out there putting maize in. You can't wait even a week, otherwise the maize doesn't finish before the cold. The other four mu and a bit I keep in cotton. That piece is the sandy ground on the edge — wheat doesn't do well there, but cotton handles it fine.

My son works in Handan at the construction, sends money home sometimes. My husband helps, he's 58 but still strong. The two daughters-in-law help when the cotton needs picking. Mostly it's me in the field day to day.

**Wheat.** Plant in October, around the Cold Dew. Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the red-bag 15-15-15 from the co-op. My husband rotaries the ground with our small tractor. Seed I buy at the town ag station, same kind everyone here plants, don't ask me the name. I irrigate before sowing so the seedbed is wet. In spring when it greens up, I irrigate again. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I scatter half a bag of urea per mu by hand, then irrigate. Maybe irrigate once more at heading if the rain doesn't come. Spray herbicide once in spring for the weeds. Harvest in June — I hire the combine, costs money but there's no other way.

**Maize.** No time to plough after wheat. I hire the no-till planter, it punches the seed in and drops compound fertilizer at the same time — about one bag per mu. When the maize is knee-high I topdress urea, maybe half a bag per mu, bury it with a hoe if I have time. Usually the July rains come, so I only irrigate if it goes dry. When I see the corn borer holes in the leaves I spray once. Harvest end of September with the combine. Yield usually better than wheat if the rains are right.

**Cotton.** More work, more money, more worry. Plant late April when the ground warms. Before planting, compound fertilizer in the rows, plough it under. The village boy lays the plastic mulch with his machine. I topdress urea twice — once at flowering, once when the bolls start forming. Irrigate once or twice in summer. The bollworm and aphids are the problem — I spray maybe four or five times through the summer when I see them, that's where the money goes. Pick starts in September, goes through October in waves. Daughters-in-law help, sometimes I pay the neighbor aunties a little to finish up.

Money is tight. Can't throw fertilizer around like the big farmers with hundreds of mu. I keep some cash back because you never know — someone gets sick, the tractor breaks. I buy fertilizer at the spring co-op sale when it's cheapest.
